Relevant text: the fence agent resource shows 'rsc_st_azure (stonith:fence_azure_arm): Stopped' with a failed start action; with missing permissions /var/log/messages shows 'Azure Error: AuthorizationFailed ... does not have authorization to perform action Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read'; the custom role (for example 'Linux Fence Agent Role') lets the agent power off and start an unhealthy VM; check it with 'fence_azure_arm --action=list --msi --resourceGroup=...'; fix by assigning the role to the affected VM, then confirm with pcs status. That a cluster without working fencing does not promote the secondary, and that turning STONITH off is unsupported and risks two primaries, are from memory of the Microsoft and Red Hat HA guides (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the SAP Basis and Azure engineer at Tarrow Chemicals, a fictional manufacturer. Production HANA (HN1) runs on hana-db1 (primary) and hana-db2 (secondary) with system replication in a RHEL Pacemaker cluster that fences with the Azure fence agent and the VMs' managed identities. Azure has scheduled maintenance on hana-db1's host at 22:30; the plan is to let the cluster move HANA to hana-db2 first.
handover: Yesterday the cloud team cleaned up role assignments in the SAP resource group.
The night's production batch runs until 06:00 and must not stop.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the two HANA nodes, the cluster's fencing resource and the identity it uses.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the cluster could not fence, what you restored and tested, and why STONITH stayed on.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects the stopped resource to the identity.
parts.modelAnswer: rsc_st_azure was Stopped after a failed start; the log showed AuthorizationFailed for the VMs' managed identities, and the activity log showed yesterday's cleanup deleting both 'Linux Fence Agent Role' assignments.

parts.label: Restored
parts.criteria: Fixes the role and proves it.
parts.modelAnswer: Re-assigned the role to each identity on both VMs, cleaned up the resource, fence_azure_arm --action=list returned both nodes, and a controlled takeover moved HANA to hana-db2 before 22:30.

parts.label: STONITH on
parts.modelAnswer: Without fencing the cluster could promote the secondary while the primary still writes, giving two primaries; it is also unsupported. The assignments are now protected from cleanup and a stopped fence alerts.

unfenced.headline: Failover without fencing is a gamble
unfenced.body: Fencing is what lets a cluster promote a secondary safely. When it fails, restore it; turning it off trades a visible problem for split brain and an unsupported configuration.

hanaDown.headline: The failover nobody could run
hanaDown.body: A Pacemaker cluster whose fence agent cannot power off nodes will not promote the secondary. Restore the agent's role before planned maintenance, and test the handover.

fenced.headline: Good: fix the fence before you need it
fenced.body: You read the fencing resource's failure, found the AuthorizationFailed, restored the role on both nodes, tested a controlled takeover, and made sure the next cleanup and the next stopped fence are caught.

scoring.modelReasoning: The fencing resource is stopped and the agent's log says AuthorizationFailed: yesterday's cleanup removed the fence role from the VMs' identities. Without fencing the cluster will not move HANA safely, and the host maintenance at 22:30 would leave it down. Re-assign the role on both VMs, clean up the resource, prove it with fence_azure_arm's list action and a controlled takeover, then guard the assignments and alert on fencing. Turning STONITH off risks two primaries; restarting Pacemaker changes nothing.
